metadata.title: Quake & Landmark Radar Mission Dataset
sources: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program (open seismic catalog)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre (open site coordinates)

properties.name: San Andreas Fault (San Francisco Bay)
properties.clue: A major right-lateral transform fault along the western coast of California, famous for the 1906 earthquake near the Golden Gate.
properties.fact: The San Andreas Fault marks the tectonic boundary between the Pacific Plate and the North American Plate.

properties.name: Pyramids of Giza
properties.clue: Ancient monumental tombs standing on a limestone plateau just west of the Nile River apex, south of the Mediterranean delta.
properties.fact: The Great Pyramid of Giza is the oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

properties.name: Mount Fuji
properties.clue: An iconic symmetrical stratovolcano on Honshu Island along the Pacific Ring of Fire, southwest of Tokyo.
properties.fact: Mount Fuji sits near a triple junction where the Amurian, Okhotsk, and Philippine Sea plates meet.

properties.name: Great Barrier Reef
properties.clue: The world's largest coral reef system, stretching over 2,300 km along the Coral Sea off the northeastern coast of Australia.
properties.fact: Comprising over 2,900 individual reefs, it is the largest living structure visible from space.

properties.name: Machu Picchu
properties.clue: A 15th-century Inca citadel perched high on an Andean mountain ridge above the Sacred Valley in southern Peru.
properties.fact: Inca engineers built earthquake-resistant ashlar masonry tailored to the active Andean subduction belt.

properties.name: North Anatolian Fault (İzmit Gulf)
properties.clue: The western segment of a 1,500 km right-lateral strike-slip fault bordering the eastern edge of the Sea of Marmara.
properties.fact: The North Anatolian Fault accommodates the westward extrusion of the Anatolian Plate relative to Eurasia.

properties.name: Mid-Atlantic Ridge (Reykjavík)
properties.clue: A subarctic volcanic island capital where the divergent boundary between the North American and Eurasian plates rises above sea level.
properties.fact: At nearby Þingvellir, the two tectonic plates drift apart by roughly 2 centimeters every year.

properties.name: Mount Everest (Himalayan Collision)
properties.clue: Earth's highest peak above sea level, uplifted by the ongoing continental collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates along the Nepal–Tibet border.
properties.fact: Tectonic uplift still pushes the Himalayas upward by several millimeters each year.

properties.name: Tohoku Subduction Zone
properties.clue: An offshore megathrust zone east of Sendai along the Japan Trench where the 2011 Mw 9.1 earthquake and tsunami originated.
properties.fact: The 2011 rupture shifted parts of Honshu island eastward by more than 2 meters.

properties.name: Strait of Gibraltar
properties.clue: A narrow maritime chokepoint separating the Iberian Peninsula from North Africa and linking the Atlantic Ocean to the Mediterranean Sea.
properties.fact: At its narrowest point, Europe and Africa are only about 14 kilometers apart.

properties.name: Valdivia Subduction Zone
properties.clue: Site of the strongest instrumentally recorded earthquake in history (Mw 9.5, 1960), along southern Chile where the Nazca Plate subducts beneath South America.
properties.fact: The 1960 Valdivia earthquake generated a trans-Pacific tsunami reaching Hawaii, Japan, and the Philippines.

properties.name: Cappadocia Volcanic Region
properties.clue: A high Central Anatolian plateau sculpted into fairy chimneys from eroded ignimbrite and volcanic tuff erupted by ancient Mount Erciyes and Hasan.
properties.fact: Soft volcanic tuff allowed ancient inhabitants to carve multi-level underground cities and rock churches.

properties.name: Sunda Megathrust (Banda Aceh)
properties.clue: Northern tip of Sumatra bordering the Indian Ocean subduction trench that triggered the devastating 2004 Mw 9.1 Indian Ocean tsunami.
properties.fact: The 2004 rupture propagated roughly 1,300 km northward along the Sunda Trench.

properties.name: Petra (Dead Sea Transform)
properties.clue: Rose-red sandstone rock-cut Nabataean city nestled in southern Jordan along the eastern flank of the Wadi Araba–Dead Sea Transform rift.
properties.fact: Petra's advanced water-conduit and dam network sustained a thriving desert metropolis.

properties.name: Mount Kilimanjaro (East African Rift)
properties.clue: Africa's highest free-standing dormant volcano, rising near the Tanzania–Kenya border along the eastern branch of the East African Rift System.
properties.fact: The East African Rift is an active continental rift slowly splitting the African Plate into the Nubian and Somali plates.
